category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient presents with a midline neck mass. During swallowing, the mass moves vertically because it is tethered by the [___] fascia, which also encloses the infrahyoid muscles.
back:
Pretracheal Fascia.
- Encloses the thyroid gland, trachea, and infrahyoid muscles.
- Attaches to laryngeal cartilages and the hyoid bone.
- Directs the movement of the strap muscles.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Describe how the Thyrohyoid muscle differs from the other strap muscles in both innervation and specific action.
back:
Innervation: C1 fibers via Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
- Action: Elevates the thyroid cartilage (larynx) or depresses the hyoid.
- Unique as it can act as a laryngeal elevator.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Distinguish between the Omohyoid and Sternohyoid based on their inferior attachments.
back:
Omohyoid: Superior border of the scapula (inferior belly).
- Sternohyoid: Posterior surface of manubrium and medial end of clavicle.
- Both insert onto the body of the hyoid bone and are supplied by ansa cervicalis.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Specify the innervation and primary attachment of the Geniohyoid muscle relative to the mandible.
back:
Innervation: C1 via Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
- Attachment: Inferior genial tubercle (mental spine) of the mandible.
- Action: Pulls the hyoid bone anteriorly and superiorly.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Nerve Supply of Mylohyoid and Anterior Digastric
front: The [___] nerve, a branch of the mandibular division (V3), provides the motor supply to both the Mylohyoid muscle and the anterior belly of the Digastric.
back:
• Mylohyoid nerve
• Derived from the inferior alveolar nerve
• Supplies muscles of the 1st pharyngeal arch

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A 25-year-old male sustains a deep neck laceration. On examination, he can elevate his hyoid but cannot depress it effectively during the final stage of swallowing. Which group of muscles is likely damaged?
back:
• Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles
• Includes: Sternohyoid, Omohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Thyrohyoid
• Function: Depress hyoid bone and larynx

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Action of Infrahyoid Muscles in Swallowing
front: Explain the role of the infrahyoid muscles in facilitating laryngeal movement during the swallowing reflex.
back:
• They fix the hyoid bone steady
• Depress the hyoid and larynx after they have been elevated by suprahyoid muscles
• Resets the airway position for breathing after deglutition

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Contrast the two bellies of the Digastric muscle regarding their embryological origin and corresponding nerve supply.
back:
• Anterior Belly: 1st pharyngeal arch; Mylohyoid nerve (V3)
• Posterior Belly: 2nd pharyngeal arch; Facial nerve (CN VII)
• Attachment: Linked by intermediate tendon to hyoid

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Identify the infrahyoid muscle that takes part of its origin from the superior border of the scapula and the suprascapular ligament.
back:
• Omohyoid muscle
• Superior belly attaches to hyoid
• Inferior belly attaches to scapula
• Joined by an intermediate tendon

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Most infrahyoid muscles are supplied by the Ansa Cervicalis (C1-C3), with the notable exception of the [___] muscle, which is supplied specifically by C1 fibers via the Hypoglossal nerve.
back:
• Thyrohyoid muscle
• Also applies to Geniohyoid (suprahyoid)
• Nerves leave CN XII as the nerve to thyrohyoid

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient presents with a midline floor-of-the-mouth weakness. During examination, the hyoid fails to move anteriorly and superiorly. This suggests a lesion involving which suprahyoid muscle and its nerve?
back:
• Geniohyoid muscle
• Nerve supply: C1 via Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
• Action: Elevates and pulls hyoid forward; depresses mandible

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Describe the coordinated mechanical action of the suprahyoid muscles when the hyoid bone is fixed by the infrahyoid group.
back:
• They act as depressors of the mandible
• Facilitates forced opening of the mouth
• Primarily involves Digastric, Mylohyoid, and Geniohyoid

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Distinguish between the superior attachments of the Sternohyoid and the Sternothyroid muscles.
back:
• Sternohyoid: Inserts on the lower border of the hyoid body
• Sternothyroid: Inserts on the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage
• Both are supplied by Ansa Cervicalis

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: List the components and the muscle it primarily tenses/elevates that forms the floor of the oral cavity.
back:
• Mylohyoid muscle
• Attachment: Mylohyoid line of mandible to hyoid body
• Action: Elevates floor of mouth and hyoid during first stage of swallowing

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Nerve supply of the Posterior Belly of Digastric
front: The posterior belly of the digastric muscle, a derivative of the second pharyngeal arch, is innervated by the [___] nerve.
back: * Facial nerve (CN VII). * Enters the muscle after emerging from the stylomastoid foramen. * Also supplies the stylohyoid muscle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient presents with difficulty depressing the mandible against resistance and an inability to elevate the floor of the mouth. Damage to the nerve supplying the [___] muscle is most likely.
back: * Mylohyoid muscle. * Innervated by the Nerve to Mylohyoid (branch of Mandibular nerve V3). * Action elevates hyoid and floor of mouth during swallowing.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Explain the mechanical role of the infrahyoid muscles during the terminal stage of swallowing (deglutition).
back: * Depress the hyoid bone and larynx. * Re-establish laryngeal position for breathing after the bolus enters the esophagus. * Steady the hyoid to provide a base for tongue movement.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Nerve supply contrast of infrahyoid muscles
front: Contrast the innervation of the Thyrohyoid muscle with that of the Sternohyoid and Omohyoid muscles.
back: * Thyrohyoid: C1 fibers via the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII). * Sternohyoid/Omohyoid: Ansa cervicalis (C1-C3 loops). * All are infrahyoid muscles but differ in nerve source.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Describe the unique attachments and structural features of the Omohyoid muscle.
back: * Origin: Superior border of the scapula (near suprascapular notch). * Insertion: Inferior border of the hyoid body. * Features: Superior and inferior bellies joined by an intermediate tendon anchored to the clavicle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Unlike most suprahyoid muscles supplied by cranial nerves, the Geniohyoid is uniquely innervated by [___] spinal nerves.
back: * C1 spinal nerves. * These fibers travel alongside the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII). * They diverge as a separate branch to reach the muscle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient has a large goiter. Superior expansion of the thyroid mass is restricted by the attachment of the [___] muscle to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
back: * Sternothyroid muscle. * Origin: Posterior surface of manubrium. * Insertion: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage. * Clinical: Forces enlarged thyroids to expand laterally or inferiorly.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: How do the suprahyoid muscles facilitate airway protection during the pharyngeal phase of swallowing?
back: * Contract to elevate the hyoid and larynx superiorly/anteriorly. * This pulls the larynx under the tongue base. * Helps the epiglottis seal the laryngeal inlet, preventing aspiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Distinguish between the Mylohyoid and Geniohyoid muscles regarding their anatomical layers in the floor of the mouth.
back: * Mylohyoid: Forms the muscular floor; more superficial (inferior). * Geniohyoid: Located superior (deep) to the mylohyoid; runs from mental spines to hyoid body.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: List the four muscles comprising the suprahyoid group and state their shared primary action on the hyoid bone.
back: * Muscles: Digastric, Stylohyoid, Mylohyoid, Geniohyoid. * Action: Elevate the hyoid bone (and larynx) during swallowing and vocalization.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Nerve Supply of the Anterior Digastric
front: The anterior belly of the digastric muscle, derived from the first pharyngeal arch, is innervated by the [___] nerve.
back:
• Nerve to mylohyoid.
• This is a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve.
• It originates from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (V3).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A surgeon performing a thyroidectomy accidentally damages the nerve supplying the thyrohyoid muscle. Identify the spinal nerve origin and the cranial nerve that carries these fibers.
back:
• Spinal nerve: C1.
• Carrier: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
• Note: Unlike other infrahyoids, it is not supplied by the ansa cervicalis.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Explain the mechanical role of the suprahyoid muscles during the first stage of deglutition (swallowing).
back:
• Elevation: They pull the hyoid bone and larynx upward and forward.
• Protection: This moves the larynx under the tongue base, assisting the epiglottis in sealing the laryngeal inlet.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Contrast the nerve supply of the anterior and posterior bellies of the digastric muscle based on their embryological origins.
back:
• Anterior Belly: Mandibular nerve (V3); derived from 1st pharyngeal arch.
• Posterior Belly: Facial nerve (VII); derived from 2nd pharyngeal arch.
• Function: Both bellies work to elevate the hyoid.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Identify the specific insertion and primary action of the sternothyroid muscle that distinguishes it from other strap muscles.
back:
• Insertion: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage (not the hyoid).
• Action: Depresses the larynx and thyroid cartilage after elevation during swallowing.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: The omohyoid, sternohyoid, and sternothyroid muscles are collectively innervated by the loop of nerves known as the [___].
back:
• Ansa cervicalis.
• Formed by the superior root (C1) and inferior root (C2, C3).
• Located within the carotid sheath.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Anatomy of the Mylohyoid and Submandibular Space
front: A patient with a submandibular space infection (Ludwig Angina) presents with a superiorly displaced tongue. Which suprahyoid muscle forms the floor of the mouth that limits the downward spread of this infection?
back:
• Mylohyoid muscle.
• It forms a muscular diaphragm between the mandible and hyoid.
• Innervation: Nerve to mylohyoid (branch of V3).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: How do the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles coordinate to facilitate forced depression of the mandible (opening the mouth against resistance)?
back:
• Fixation: Infrahyoid muscles contract to stabilize/fix the hyoid bone.
• Leverage: With the hyoid anchored, the suprahyoids (digastric, mylohyoid, geniohyoid) pull the mandible downward.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Distinguish between the superior and inferior bellies of the omohyoid muscle regarding their distal attachments.
back:
• Superior Belly: Attaches to the lower border of the hyoid bone.
• Inferior Belly: Attaches to the superior border of the scapula near the suprascapular notch.
• Connection: Linked by an intermediate tendon.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Specify the nerve supply and primary action of the geniohyoid muscle.
back:
• Nerve: C1 fibers via the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
• Action: Elevates the hyoid and draws it forward; also assists in depressing the mandible when the hyoid is fixed.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: The posterior belly of the digastric muscle is innervated by the [___] nerve.
back: Facial nerve (CN VII).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Functional Anatomy of the Oral Floor
front: A 45-year-old patient presents with difficulty initiating the first stage of swallowing. Examination reveals weakness in the floor of the mouth. Which suprahyoid muscle is likely involved, and what is its innervation?
back: The Mylohyoid muscle. It is supplied by the nerve to the mylohyoid, a branch of the mandibular nerve (CN V3).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Explain the role of the infrahyoid (strap) muscles in stabilizing the hyoid bone during tongue movements.
back:
*   They depress and steady the hyoid bone. 
*   This provides a firm base for the suprahyoid muscles to act upon during speech and tongue protrusion.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient suffers a high-neck trauma involving the C1 spinal nerve before it joins the ansa cervicalis. Contrast the effect on the Thyrohyoid muscle versus the Sternohyoid muscle.
back:
*   Thyrohyoid: Paralyzed (specifically supplied by C1 fibers via CN XII).
*   Sternohyoid: Remains functional if C2/C3 components of ansa cervicalis are intact.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Describe the functional sequence of the hyoid muscles during the swallowing process.
back:
1. Suprahyoid muscles: Elevate hyoid/larynx to protect the airway.
2. Infrahyoid muscles: Depress the hyoid/larynx back to neutral position for respiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: The only infrahyoid muscle that attaches directly to the thyroid cartilage rather than the hyoid bone is the [___].
back: Sternothyroid muscle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient exhibits an inability to depress the hyoid bone, but laryngeal elevation is normal. A lesion of the ansa cervicalis is suspected. Which group of muscles is primarily affected?
back: Infrahyoid (strap) muscles (Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: How does the structural arrangement of the omohyoid's intermediate tendon facilitate its action on the internal jugular vein?
back:
*   The tendon is bound to the clavicle by deep fascia.
*   Contraction tenses the fascia, preventing the internal jugular vein from collapsing during deep inspiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Contrast the innervation of the anterior belly of the digastric muscle with that of the geniohyoid muscle.
back:
*   Anterior Digastric: Nerve to Mylohyoid (CN V3).
*   Geniohyoid: C1 fibers via the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Identify the specific suprahyoid muscle that originates from the styloid process and splits around the intermediate tendon of the digastric.
back: Stylohyoid muscle.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The inferior root (radix inferior) of the ansa cervicalis is formed by the union of the anterior rami of spinal nerves [___].
back:
• C2 and C3
• These rami join to form the descendens cervicalis
• It winds around the internal jugular vein to join the superior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A surgeon performing a carotid endarterectomy identifies a nerve loop superficial to the internal jugular vein. If this structure is sacrificed, which group of muscles will lose motor innervation?
back:
• Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles
• Specifically: Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid
• Note: Thyrohyoid is spared as it is supplied directly by C1 via CN XII.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the anatomical pathway by which C1 spinal nerve fibers reach the superior root of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• C1 fibers join the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) shortly after it leaves the skull
• They travel with CN XII briefly
• They leave as the descendens hypoglossi (superior root).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the nerve supply of the Thyrohyoid muscle with that of the Sternothyroid muscle regarding their relationship to the ansa cervicalis loop.
back:
• Thyrohyoid: Supplied by C1 fibers via CN XII directly (not part of the loop)
• Sternothyroid: Supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop (C1, C2, C3).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: State the precise location of the ansa cervicalis in relation to the carotid sheath.
back:
• Embedded in the anterior wall of the carotid sheath
• Located within the carotid triangle of the neck
• Lies superficial to the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis, also known as the [___], is primarily composed of fibers from the C1 spinal nerve.
back:
• Descendens hypoglossi
• It descends between the internal carotid artery and internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient presents with weakness in depressing the hyoid bone after a deep neck injury. Anatomically, the nerve loop responsible for this action is formed by the cervical plexus and travels with which cranial nerve?
back:
• Hypoglossal Nerve (CN XII)
• The C1 fibers use CN XII as a hitchhiking pathway to form the superior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the functional distribution of the ansa cervicalis regarding the Omohyoid muscle.
back:
• Supplies both the superior and inferior bellies
• Branch to the superior belly arises from the superior root
• Branch to the inferior belly arises from the loop itself.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the descendens hypoglossi and descendens cervicalis based on their spinal nerve contributions.
back:
• Descendens hypoglossi (Superior root): C1 fibers only
• Descendens cervicalis (Inferior root): C2 and C3 fibers.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the spinal cord segments that provide the motor outflow for the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• C1, C2, and C3
• These segments contribute to the anterior rami that form the cervical plexus.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
coreConcept: Nerve Supply Exception of Infrahyoid Muscles
front: While most infrahyoid muscles are supplied by the ansa cervicalis, the [___] muscle is uniquely innervated by fibers from the C1 ventral ramus traveling via the hypoglossal nerve.
back:
The Thyrohyoid muscle.
- Part of the infrahyoid (strap) group.
- Action: Depresses hyoid or elevates larynx.
- Innervated by C1 via CN XII, similar to Geniohyoid.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient presents with difficulty in the initial stage of deglutition. Examination shows limited upward movement of the hyoid bone. Impairment of which functional muscle group is most likely responsible?
back:
Suprahyoid muscles.
- Includes: Digastric, Stylohyoid, Mylohyoid, and Geniohyoid.
- Primary Action: Elevate the hyoid bone and larynx during swallowing and speech.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Explain the role of the Mylohyoid muscle in the structural anatomy of the oral cavity and its primary action.
back:
- Structure: Forms the dynamic floor of the mouth.
- Action: Elevates the floor of the mouth and hyoid bone during the first stage of deglutition.
- Innervation: Nerve to mylohyoid (branch of V3).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Contrast the embryonic origin and respective nerve supply of the anterior and posterior bellies of the digastric muscle.
back:
- Anterior Belly: Derived from 1st pharyngeal arch; supplied by Nerve to Mylohyoid (V3).
- Posterior Belly: Derived from 2nd pharyngeal arch; supplied by Facial Nerve (VII).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: List the two infrahyoid muscles that attach directly to the thyroid cartilage and specify their actions.
back:
- Sternothyroid: Depresses the larynx.
- Thyrohyoid: Elevates the larynx or depresses the hyoid.
- Both attach to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: The [___] muscle is a strap muscle of the neck consisting of two bellies connected by an intermediate tendon, which is anchored to the clavicle by a fascial sling.
back:
Omohyoid muscle.
- Inferior belly: Arises from the scapula.
- Superior belly: Attaches to the hyoid bone.
- Innervation: Ansa cervicalis (C1-C3).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: During a surgical procedure in the carotid triangle, the surgeon identifies a nerve loop embedded in the carotid sheath. Accidental ligation of this loop would paralyze which specific muscles?
back:
The Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles.
- Specifically: Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid.
- The structure is the Ansa Cervicalis (Superior root C1, Inferior root C2-C3).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Identify the innervation of the Geniohyoid muscle and describe its mechanical effect on the hyoid bone.
back:
- Innervation: C1 fibers via the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
- Action: Pulls the hyoid bone anteriorly and upward.
- Location: Lies superior to the mylohyoid muscle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Contrast the Sternohyoid and Sternothyroid muscles regarding their superior attachments.
back:
- Sternohyoid: Attaches to the lower border of the hyoid bone.
- Sternothyroid: Attaches to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
- Both are supplied by the ansa cervicalis.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Which suprahyoid muscle originates from the styloid process and splits around the intermediate tendon of the digastric?
back:
Stylohyoid muscle.
- Origin: Styloid process of temporal bone.
- Nerve Supply: Facial nerve (VII).
- Action: Pulls hyoid bone upward and backward during swallowing.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis is primarily formed by fibers from the [___] spinal nerve that temporarily 'hitchhike' with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
back: C1 (Anterior ramus). It leaves CN XII as the *descendens hypoglossi* to join the inferior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A surgeon performing a carotid endarterectomy identifies a nerve loop lying superficial to the carotid sheath. Damage to this structure would likely paralyze which group of neck muscles?
back: Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles. These include the sternohyoid, sternothyroid, and omohyoid (both bellies).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the role of the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) in the formation of the ansa cervicalis.
back: It acts as a physical carrier for C1 fibers. These fibers travel briefly with CN XII before branching off as the superior root (*descendens hypoglossi*).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the spinal nerve contributions of the superior root versus the inferior root of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Superior Root: Derived from C1.
• Inferior Root: Derived from C2 and C3 (Anterior rami).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: List the three specific infrahyoid muscles supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop.
back:
• Sternohyoid.
• Sternothyroid.
• Omohyoid (Superior and inferior bellies).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The ansa cervicalis is anatomically situated within the carotid triangle, typically located superficial to or embedded in the anterior wall of the [___].
back: Carotid sheath. It specifically lies over the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient suffers a deep laceration in the carotid triangle. If the thyrohyoid muscle remains functional but the sternohyoid is paralyzed, where is the most likely site of the lesion?
back: The ansa cervicalis loop itself. Thyrohyoid is spared as it is supplied directly by C1 fibers via CN XII, not via the ansa loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the assembly of the 'ansa' (loop) in relation to the internal jugular vein.
back: The superior root (C1) and inferior root (C2-C3) descend and unite in a loop shape, usually crossing the anterior surface of the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the ansa cervicalis and the ansa subclavia regarding their parent nervous system divisions.
back:
• Ansa cervicalis: Somatic (Cervical plexus C1-C3).
• Ansa subclavia: Autonomic (Sympathetic trunk/ganglia).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the cervical plexus branch that specifically constitutes the inferior root of the ansa cervicalis.
back: Descendens cervicalis. It is formed by the union of rami from C2 and C3.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: The [___] muscle is a suprahyoid muscle that originates from the inferior mental spine of the mandible and is innervated by C1 fibers hitchhiking with the hypoglossal nerve.
back:
• Geniohyoid muscle
• Action: Elevates and pulls the hyoid bone anteriorly
• Innervation: C1 via Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
• Role: Shortens the floor of the mouth

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A patient exhibits difficulty depressing the larynx after swallowing. Examination reveals a lesion in the ansa cervicalis. Identify the group of muscles affected and their general function.
back:
• Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles
• Includes: Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid
• Nerve: Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3)
• Action: Depress the hyoid bone and larynx

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Describe the specific mechanical role of the Sternothyroid muscle during the terminal stages of deglutition.
back:
• Depresses the larynx
• Attachment: Posterior manubrium to the oblique line of thyroid cartilage
• Nerve: Ansa cervicalis
• Significance: Resets laryngeal position for breathing

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Contrast the embryological origins and resulting nerve supplies of the two bellies of the Digastric muscle.
back:
• Anterior Belly: 1st pharyngeal arch; Nerve to Mylohyoid (V3)
• Posterior Belly: 2nd pharyngeal arch; Facial nerve (CN VII)
• Common Action: Depresses mandible or elevates hyoid

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Identify the only infrahyoid muscle that is not supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop.
back:
• Thyrohyoid muscle
• Innervation: C1 nerve fibers via Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
• Action: Depresses hyoid or elevates thyroid cartilage
• Location: Deep to the sternohyoid

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: The [___] muscle consists of two bellies connected by an intermediate tendon and originates from the superior border of the scapula to insert on the hyoid bone.
back:
• Omohyoid muscle
• Nerve: Ansa cervicalis (C1–C3)
• Action: Depresses and retracts the hyoid bone
• Landmark: Divides the neck's posterior triangle

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: A 45-year-old male undergoes a parotidectomy. Post-operatively, he has difficulty elevating the hyoid and retracting it. The muscle arising from the styloid process is paralyzed. Name the muscle and nerve.
back:
• Stylohyoid muscle
• Nerve: Facial nerve (CN VII)
• Action: Elevates and retracts the hyoid bone
• Attachment: Styloid process to the hyoid body

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Explain the anatomical pathway of the nerve fibers supplying the Geniohyoid and Thyrohyoid muscles.
back:
• Origin: C1 spinal nerve ventral rami
• Pathway: Fibers join the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
• Distribution: Leave CN XII as distinct muscular branches
• Distinction: Do not join the ansa cervicalis

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Distinguish between the Sternohyoid and Sternothyroid based on their superior insertions.
back:
• Sternohyoid: Inserts on the lower border of the hyoid bone
• Sternothyroid: Inserts on the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage
• Nerve: Both supplied by Ansa Cervicalis

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles of neck
front: Identify the nerve that provides motor supply to both the Mylohyoid muscle and the anterior belly of the Digastric.
back:
• Nerve to Mylohyoid
• Source: Inferior alveolar nerve (Mandibular division of CN V)
• Action: Elevates the floor of the mouth
• Embryology: 1st pharyngeal arch derivative

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The ansa cervicalis is a nerve loop typically embedded in the anterior wall of the [___] within the carotid triangle.
back:
Carotid sheath.
• It lies superficial to the internal jugular vein.
• It is situated deep to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A surgeon performing a radical neck dissection accidentally severs the nerve loop crossing the internal jugular vein. Which group of muscles will likely lose motor function?
back:
Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles:
• Sternohyoid
• Sternothyroid
• Omohyoid (both bellies).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the neural formation of the superior root (descendens hypoglossi) of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Formed by fibers from the C1 ventral ramus.
• Fibers hitchhike with the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
• They descend from CN XII as it crosses the internal carotid artery.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the innervation of the thyrohyoid muscle with that of the sternothyroid muscle.
back:
• Thyrohyoid: C1 fibers via CN XII (nerve to thyrohyoid).
• Sternothyroid: Nerve loop of the ansa cervicalis (C1-C3).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the specific cervical spinal nerve rami that contribute to the formation of the inferior root (descendens cervicalis).
back:
• Ventral rami of C2 and C3.
• These rami unite to form the inferior root.
• It passes anteriorly to join the superior root over the IJV.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The ansa cervicalis is derived from the [___] plexus and provides motor supply to the strap muscles.
back:
Cervical plexus.
• Specifically from the ventral rami of C1, C2, and C3 spinal nerves.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient exhibits weakness in depressing the hyoid bone during swallowing, but the thyrohyoid muscle is functioning normally. Which neural structure is most likely damaged?
back:
Ansa cervicalis (main loop).
• Thyrohyoid receives fibers directly from C1 via CN XII.
• Other strap muscles rely on the full ansa loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Trace the path of the superior root from its origin to its junction with the inferior root.
back:
• Arises from C1.
• Joins CN XII near the base of skull.
• Leaves CN XII in the carotid triangle.
• Descends anterior to the carotid sheath to join the inferior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the ansa cervicalis and the ansa subclavia regarding their parent nervous system divisions.
back:
• Ansa cervicalis: Somatic nervous system (Cervical plexus).
• Ansa subclavia: Autonomic nervous system (Sympathetic trunk).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: In what specific anatomic triangle of the neck is the ansa cervicalis primarily found?
back:
Carotid triangle.
• It is bounded by the sternocleidomastoid, omohyoid (superior belly), and posterior belly of digastric.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis, also known as the descendens hypoglossi, consists of fibers from the [___] spinal nerve that hitchhike with Cranial Nerve XII.
back:
• C1 (First cervical nerve).
• These fibers eventually leave CN XII to form the loop's upper limb.
• Supplies the superior belly of omohyoid.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient undergoes a radical neck dissection. Post-operatively, they exhibit weakness in hyoid depression. Intraoperatively, a nerve loop on the anterior carotid sheath was damaged. Identify the structure.
back:
• Ansa cervicalis.
• Location: Embedded in the anterior wall of the carotid sheath.
• Function: Motor supply to the infrahyoid (strap) muscles.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the neural formation of the inferior root (descendens cervicalis) of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Formed by anterior rami of C2 and C3.
• It descends posterior to the internal jugular vein.
• Joins the superior root to complete the loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the nerve supply of the thyrohyoid muscle with that of the sternohyoid muscle regarding their relationship to the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Sternohyoid: Supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop (C1-C3).
• Thyrohyoid: Supplied directly by C1 fibers traveling with CN XII (bypasses the ansa loop).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: List the specific infrahyoid muscles innervated by branches from the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Sternohyoid.
• Sternothyroid.
• Omohyoid (both superior and inferior bellies).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The ansa cervicalis typically lies superficial to the [___] and the common carotid artery within the carotid triangle.
back:
• Internal Jugular Vein (IJV).
• It is a key landmark during surgeries involving the carotid sheath or deep neck structures.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
coreConcept: Functional Classification of Cervical Plexus Branches
front: A surgeon identifying the 'nerve point' of the neck (Erb's point) notices several cutaneous branches. How does the ansa cervicalis differ from these branches in terms of function and depth?
back:
• Function: Ansa is purely motor (GSE); Erb's point branches are sensory.
• Depth: Ansa is deep (carotid sheath); Erb's branches are superficial to sternocleidomastoid.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the anatomical course of the ansa cervicalis loop relative to the omohyoid muscle.
back:
• The loop typically sits superior to the intermediate tendon of the omohyoid.
• Branches descend from the loop to supply the inferior belly.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the origin of the fibers supplying the geniohyoid and those supplying the sternothyroid.
back:
• Geniohyoid: C1 via CN XII (not via ansa loop).
• Sternothyroid: C1, C2, and C3 via the ansa cervicalis loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: State the functional purpose of the infrahyoid muscles innervated by the ansa cervicalis during the final stage of swallowing.
back:
• Depress the hyoid bone.
• Steady the hyoid to provide a firm base for the tongue.
• Help lower the larynx after elevation.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis is composed of fibers from the [___] spinal nerve that travel briefly with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
back: * C1 anterior rami. * These fibers leave the hypoglossal nerve to descend as the descendens hypoglossi. * They eventually unite with the inferior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient undergoing carotid artery surgery suffers an injury to a nerve loop located superficial to the internal jugular vein. Post-operatively, they have difficulty depressing the hyoid bone. Identify the injured structure.
back: * Ansa cervicalis. * This nerve loop (C1-C3) provides motor supply to the infrahyoid (strap) muscles. * It is frequently found within or on the carotid sheath.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain how the inferior root of the ansa cervicalis is formed and its subsequent anatomical union.
back: * Formation: Formed by the union of rami from C2 and C3 spinal nerves. * Union: It descends behind the internal jugular vein to join the superior root (C1). * Result: Forms a loop superficial to the vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the innervation of the thyrohyoid muscle with that of the sternohyoid muscle.
back: * Thyrohyoid: Supplied directly by C1 fibers via the hypoglossal nerve (not the ansa loop). * Sternohyoid: Supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop (C1, C2, and C3).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the three infrahyoid muscles specifically innervated by the ansa cervicalis.
back: * Sternohyoid. * Sternothyroid. * Omohyoid (both the superior and inferior bellies).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The ansa cervicalis is typically found embedded within the anterior wall of the [___] inside the carotid triangle of the neck.
back: * Carotid sheath. * It is positioned superficial to the internal jugular vein. * It serves as a key landmark during neck dissections.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A surgeon is performing a radical neck dissection. To preserve the motor function of the omohyoid muscle, which specific neural loop must be identified and protected?
back: * Ansa cervicalis. * It provides the sole motor supply to the omohyoid. * The loop consists of a superior (C1) and inferior (C2-C3) root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the spatial relationship between the ansa cervicalis and the internal jugular vein (IJV).
back: * Superior root: Descends anterior to the IJV. * Inferior root: Passes lateral/posterior to the IJV before looping forward. * The loop itself sits superficial to the IJV.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the terms 'Descendens hypoglossi' and 'Descendens cervicalis'.
back: * Descendens hypoglossi: The superior root of ansa cervicalis (C1 fibers). * Descendens cervicalis: The inferior root of ansa cervicalis (C2 and C3 fibers).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Specify the spinal nerve levels that contribute to the entire ansa cervicalis complex.
back: * Anterior rami of C1, C2, and C3. * C1 contributes via the superior root. * C2 and C3 contribute via the inferior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root (descendens hypoglossi) of the ansa cervicalis is formed by fibers from the [___] spinal nerve that hitchhike along the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
back:
• C1 spinal nerve.
• It descends from the hypoglossal nerve to join the inferior root.
• It carries only motor fibers.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: During a carotid endarterectomy, a nerve loop lying on the anterior wall of the carotid sheath is accidentally injured. Explain the resulting motor deficit.
back:
• Paralysis of infrahyoid (strap) muscles.
• Specifically: Sternohyoid, sternothyroid, and omohyoid.
• Result: Impaired hyoid bone and larynx stabilization during swallowing.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the specific neural contributions to the inferior root (descendens cervicalis) of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Formed by branches from the cervical plexus.
• Derived from the anterior rami of C2 and C3.
• It joins the superior root anterior to the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the nerve supply of the thyrohyoid muscle with that of the omohyoid muscle in relation to the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Thyrohyoid: Supplied by C1 fibers via CN XII (does not pass through the ansa loop).
• Omohyoid: Supplied directly by the ansa cervicalis (C1-C3 loop).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the precise anatomical location of the ansa cervicalis loop in relation to the carotid sheath.
back:
• Located within the anterior wall of the carotid sheath.
• Situated superficial (anterior) to the internal jugular vein.
• Located at the level of the cricoid cartilage.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The [___] is the only infrahyoid muscle NOT supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop, instead receiving C1 fibers directly via the hypoglossal nerve.
back:
• Thyrohyoid muscle.
• (Geniohyoid is also supplied by C1 via CN XII, but is a suprahyoid muscle).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient presents with difficulty in laryngeal depression after a trauma involving the carotid triangle. If the ansa cervicalis is damaged, which three strap muscles are affected?
back:
• Sternohyoid.
• Sternothyroid.
• Omohyoid (superior and inferior bellies).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the physiological mechanism by which C1 fibers are distributed to both the ansa cervicalis and the geniohyoid muscle.
back:
• C1 fibers join the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) shortly after exiting the skull.
• Some fibers leave as the superior root of ansa cervicalis.
• Other fibers stay with CN XII to reach the geniohyoid and thyrohyoid.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the ansa cervicalis and the ansa subclavia regarding their location and function.
back:
• Ansa Cervicalis: Nerve loop C1-C3 in carotid triangle; motor to strap muscles.
• Ansa Subclavia: Sympathetic loop around the subclavian artery; connects middle and inferior cervical ganglia.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Specify the cervical plexus rami that form the 'loop' structure of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• Superior root: C1.
• Inferior root: C2 and C3.
• Result: A nerve loop supplying the infrahyoid muscles.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis is composed of fibers from the [___] spinal nerve that travel briefly alongside the hypoglossal nerve.
back:
C1 (First cervical nerve).
* These fibers leave the hypoglossal nerve as the descendens hypoglossi.
* It forms the upper limb of the loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: During a radical neck dissection, a surgeon identifies a nerve loop embedded in the anterior wall of the carotid sheath. Damage to this structure would paralyze which group of muscles?
back:
Infrahyoid (Strap) muscles.
* Specifically: Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid.
* Exception: Thyrohyoid is spared as it is supplied directly by C1 via CN XII.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the assembly of the inferior root (descendens cervicalis) of the ansa cervicalis and its relationship to the internal jugular vein.
back:
* Formed by the union of C2 and C3 ventral rami.
* It descends posterior or lateral to the internal jugular vein.
* It سپس curves forward to join the superior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the nerve supply of the Thyrohyoid muscle with that of the Omohyoid muscle.
back:
* Thyrohyoid: C1 fibers traveling with the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
* Omohyoid: Branches directly from the Ansa Cervicalis loop (C1-C3).
* Clinical note: Thyrohyoid is not innervated by the loop itself.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: List the specific spinal nerve rami that contribute to the formation of the entire ansa cervicalis loop.
back:
* Anterior rami of C1.
* Anterior rami of C2.
* Anterior rami of C3.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The [___] root of the ansa cervicalis is also referred to in older texts as the 'descendens hypoglossi.'
back:
Superior root.
* Derived from C1.
* Runs in the anterior wall of the carotid sheath.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient presents with difficulty depressing the hyoid bone during the final stages of swallowing. Anatomically, this suggests a lesion to the nerve loop located superficial to the [___].
back:
Internal Jugular Vein.
* The ansa cervicalis is located anterior to this vein within the carotid sheath.
* It supplies the muscles responsible for hyoid depression.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the physiological significance of the C1 fibers that do NOT join the ansa cervicalis loop but continue with the hypoglossal nerve.
back:
* They supply the Geniohyoid muscle.
* They supply the Thyrohyoid muscle.
* These fibers provide motor innervation via CN XII hitchhiking.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish the 'descendens hypoglossi' from the 'descendens cervicalis' based on their respective positions relative to the carotid artery.
back:
* Descendens hypoglossi (Superior): Lies anterior to the internal and common carotid arteries.
* Descendens cervicalis (Inferior): Lies lateral/posterior to the internal jugular vein before joining the loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the primary function of the muscles supplied by the ansa cervicalis during the act of deglutition.
back:
Depression of the hyoid bone and larynx.
* This occurs after the larynx has been elevated during swallowing.
* Stabilizes the hyoid for tongue movement.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The [___] spinal nerve provides the fibers that form the superior root (descendens hypoglossi) of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
C1
- Fibers travel briefly with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
- Leaves CN XII to form the superior limb of the loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A surgeon performing a radical neck dissection identifies a nerve loop lying on the anterior surface of the carotid sheath. Damage to this structure would paralyze which specific group of muscles?
back:
Infrahyoid (Strap) Muscles
- Specifically: Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid
- Sparing: Thyrohyoid (supplied by C1 via CN XII).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the formation of the inferior root (descendens cervicalis) of the ansa cervicalis.
back:
Union of C2 and C3
- Formed by branches from the anterior rami of C2 and C3 spinal nerves
- Passes around the lateral side of the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient presents with weakness in hyoid depression after surgery. Contrast the source of innervation for the omohyoid muscle with that of the geniohyoid muscle.
back:
Omohyoid vs Geniohyoid
- Omohyoid: Ansa cervicalis (C1-C3)
- Geniohyoid: C1 fibers traveling with the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Specify the anatomical location of the ansa cervicalis loop within the subdivisions of the neck.
back:
Carotid Triangle
- Lies on or embedded within the anterior wall of the carotid sheath
- Usually superficial to the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis is clinically referred to as the [___] due to its initial pathway alongside the 12th cranial nerve.
back:
Descendens hypoglossi
- Composed purely of C1 spinal nerve fibers
- Joins the inferior root to complete the loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
coreConcept: Clinical Localization of Ansa Cervicalis Injury
front: Following a deep laceration in the carotid triangle, a patient is unable to depress their hyoid bone, but tongue movements are perfectly preserved. Which structure is likely injured?
back:
Ansa cervicalis
- Normal tongue movement indicates CN XII is intact
- Hyoid depression loss confirms injury to strap muscle innervation.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient undergoes neck surgery and loses motor supply to the sternohyoid and sternothyroid. Sparing of the thyrohyoid suggests the lesion is distal to which nerve junction?
back:
Hypoglossal-C1 Junction
- Thyrohyoid is supplied by C1 fibers before they form the ansa cervicalis
- This sparing suggests a specific injury to the ansa cervicalis loop itself.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish the 'Superior Root' from the 'Inferior Root' of the ansa cervicalis based on their spinal nerve origins.
back:
Spinal Origins
- Superior Root: C1 fibers only
- Inferior Root: C2 and C3 fibers.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Which muscle of the infrahyoid group is the only one NOT supplied by the ansa cervicalis?
back:
Thyrohyoid
- Innervated by C1 fibers via the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
- All other strap muscles (Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, Omohyoid) are supplied by the ansa.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis is primarily formed by fibers from the [___] spinal nerve that momentarily travel with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
back:
C1 (First cervical nerve).
- It leaves CN XII as the 'descendens hypoglossi'.
- Joins the inferior root to form the ansa loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
coreConcept: Clinical Presentation of Ansa Cervicalis Injury
front: A surgeon performing a thyroidectomy accidentally damages a nerve loop embedded in the anterior wall of the carotid sheath. Post-operatively, the patient exhibits weakness in depressing the hyoid bone. Identify the structure.
back:
Ansa cervicalis.
- Location: Anterior wall of carotid sheath.
- Roots: Superior (C1) and Inferior (C2-C3).
- Function: Motor supply to infrahyoid (strap) muscles.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the mechanism by which C1 fibers participate in the ansa cervicalis despite initially appearing within the hypoglossal nerve.
back:
C1 fibers 'hitchhike' with CN XII.
- They exit CN XII in the carotid triangle.
- Descend as the superior root (descendens hypoglossi).
- Fuse with C2-C3 roots superficial to the internal jugular vein.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A patient presents with paralysis of the omohyoid and sternothyroid muscles, but the thyrohyoid muscle remains functional. Contrast the nerve supply of these muscles to explain this finding.
back:
Omohyoid/Sternothyroid: Supplied by the ansa cervicalis (C1-C3).
- Thyrohyoid: Supplied directly by C1 via CN XII before the ansa forms.
- Lesion of the ansa loop spares thyrohyoid function.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Specify the precise anatomical relationship between the ansa cervicalis and the internal jugular vein.
back:
Located superficial to the internal jugular vein.
- Often embedded in the fascia of the carotid sheath.
- Situated within the carotid triangle of the neck.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The inferior root of the ansa cervicalis, also termed the descendens cervicalis, is formed by the union of the [___] and [___] spinal nerve rami.
back:
C2 and C3.
- These fibers arise from the cervical plexus.
- They wind around the internal jugular vein to join the superior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: During a nerve reconstructive procedure for laryngeal paralysis, the surgeon selects a nearby motor branch for reinnervation. Why is the ansa cervicalis a preferred candidate for this transfer?
back:
Proximity to the larynx.
- Reliable motor axon source (C1-C3).
- Minimal functional deficit after donor sacrifice (strap muscle compensation).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the specific distribution of the superior and inferior roots to the two bellies of the omohyoid muscle.
back:
Superior root: Supplies the superior belly.
- Ansa loop/Inferior root: Supplies the inferior belly.
- This illustrates the complex motor distribution of the C1-C3 plexus.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the ansa cervicalis roots based on their origin from the cervical plexus and their 'hitchhiking' status.
back:
Superior root: C1 only; hitchhikes with CN XII.
- Inferior root: C2 and C3; direct branches from cervical plexus.
- Union: Forms the characteristic nerve loop anterior to the great vessels.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: List the three primary infrahyoid muscles supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop proper.
back:
Sternohyoid.
- Sternothyroid.
- Omohyoid (both bellies).
- Note: Thyrohyoid is supplied by C1 via CN XII, not the loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The superior root of the ansa cervicalis, which contains fibers from the C1 spinal nerve, is also known as the [___].
back:
• Descendens hypoglossi.
• It consists of C1 fibers that briefly hitchhike with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
• It descends to join the inferior root superficial to the carotid sheath.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: A 45-year-old male undergoing a carotid endarterectomy sustains an injury to a nerve loop lying superficial to the internal jugular vein. He subsequently exhibits weakness in depressing his hyoid bone. Identify the nerve and the muscles it innervates.
back:
• Ansa cervicalis.
• Muscles: Sternohyoid, sternothyroid, and omohyoid (both bellies).
• Function: These infrahyoid muscles depress the hyoid bone and larynx after elevation during swallowing.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Explain the neural pathway by which C1 spinal nerve fibers reach the infrahyoid muscles through the ansa cervicalis.
back:
• C1 fibers join the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) near the skull base.
• Most fibers leave CN XII as the superior root (descendens hypoglossi).
• These fibers then loop to join C2-C3 roots to form the ansa loop.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Contrast the innervation of the thyrohyoid muscle with the sternohyoid muscle, specifically regarding their relationship to the ansa cervicalis loop.
back:
• Sternohyoid: Innervated directly by the ansa cervicalis loop (C1-C3).
• Thyrohyoid: Innervated by C1 fibers via CN XII, branching off independently after the superior root has already descended.
• Both use C1 fibers but via different branching points.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the specific spinal nerve rami that contribute to the formation of the descendens cervicalis (inferior root).
back:
• Ventral rami of C2 and C3.
• These fibers merge and descend, typically winding around the lateral aspect of the internal jugular vein before joining the superior root.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: The ansa cervicalis is anatomically situated within the anterior triangle of the neck, typically embedded in or superficial to the [___] sheath.
back:
• Carotid sheath.
• It is specifically related to the anterior wall of the sheath.
• It lies superficial to the internal jugular vein and common carotid artery.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: During a radical neck dissection, a surgeon identifies a nerve loop in the carotid triangle. If this loop is sacrificed, which muscle responsible for stabilizing the hyoid during tongue movement will remain functional due to its direct C1 supply?
back:
• Thyrohyoid muscle.
• It is the only infrahyoid muscle not supplied by the ansa cervicalis loop.
• It receives C1 fibers directly from the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Describe the functional role of the ansa cervicalis in the mechanics of deglutition (swallowing).
back:
• It provides motor supply to the strap muscles.
• These muscles depress the larynx and hyoid bone.
• This action resets the airway and facilitates the reopening of the pharynx after the bolus passes.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Distinguish between the superior and inferior roots of the ansa cervicalis based on their constituent spinal nerves and cranial nerve associations.
back:
• Superior Root: C1 fibers; travels with the Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII).
• Inferior Root: C2 and C3 fibers; arises directly from the cervical plexus.
• Together they form a loop (ansa) usually at the level of the cricoid.

category: Describe the location, formation and distribution of ansa cervicalis
front: Identify the primary muscles supplied by the ansa cervicalis and state their collective classification.
back:
• Muscles: Sternohyoid, Sternothyroid, and Omohyoid.
• Classification: Infrahyoid muscles (or 'strap' muscles).
• Note: These muscles are key landmarks in the anterior triangle of the neck.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
coreConcept: Common Motor Supply of SCM and Trapezius
front: Both the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles receive their primary motor innervation from the [___] nerve.
back: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: A neonate presents with a fixed head tilt toward the left shoulder and the face rotated toward the right. This condition, congenital torticollis, results from fibrosis and shortening of the [___] muscle.
back: Left Sternocleidomastoid (SCM).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Explain the mechanical difference in head movement when the sternocleidomastoid contracts unilaterally versus bilaterally.
back:
• Unilateral: Tilts head to same side; rotates face to opposite side.
• Bilateral: Flexes the neck (draws head forward) and assists in forced inspiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
coreConcept: Sensory Innervation of Lateral Neck Muscles
front: Distinguish the cervical spinal nerve contributions to the sensory/proprioceptive supply of the sternocleidomastoid from those of the trapezius.
back:
• Sternocleidomastoid: C2 and C3.
• Trapezius: C3 and C4.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
coreConcept: Functional Role of Trapezius in Shoulder Girdle
front: Identify the specific action of the trapezius muscle required to allow the arm to be abducted above the horizontal plane (90 degrees).
back: Upward rotation of the scapula (coordinated with the serratus anterior).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The superior attachment (origin) of the trapezius muscle includes the medial third of the [___], the external occipital protuberance, and the ligamentum nuchae.
back: Superior nuchal line.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Following a lymph node biopsy in the posterior triangle, a patient is unable to shrug their shoulder. This indicates damage to the nerve supplying the [___].
back: Trapezius (Spinal Accessory Nerve).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Describe how the sternocleidomastoid functions as an accessory muscle of inspiration during respiratory distress.
back: With the head fixed, it elevates the sternum and clavicles to increase the anteroposterior diameter of the thorax.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Contrast the origins of the two heads of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
back:
• Sternal head: Rounded tendon from the manubrium sterni.
• Clavicular head: Fleshy fibers from the medial third of the clavicle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: List the three specific bony sites of insertion for the trapezius muscle.
back:
• Lateral third of the clavicle.
• Acromion of the scapula.
• Spine of the scapula.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The motor supply of the Sternocleidomastoid muscle is provided by the [___] nerve.
back: The spinal accessory nerve (CN XI). Proprioception is provided by the anterior rami of C2 and C3.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: A 2-week-old infant presents with the head tilted to the right and the chin rotated to the left. A firm mass is felt in the neck. Identify the most likely affected muscle.
back: Sternocleidomastoid (SCM). This is Congenital Torticollis (Wry Neck), often caused by birth trauma leading to fibrosis and muscle shortening.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Explain the mechanical result of the Sternocleidomastoid muscle during bilateral contraction.
back: Flexion of the cervical vertebral column and extension of the head at the atlanto-occipital joints. It also serves as an accessory muscle of forced inspiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Contrast the proprioceptive nerve supply of the Sternocleidomastoid with that of the Trapezius muscle.
back: SCM receives proprioceptive fibers from C2 and C3 spinal nerves. Trapezius receives proprioceptive fibers from C3 and C4 spinal nerves. Both share CN XI for motor supply.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Specify the attachments of the superior (upper) fibers of the Trapezius muscle.
back: Origin: External occipital protuberance, medial third of superior nuchal line, and ligamentum nuchae. Insertion: Lateral third of the clavicle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The Sternocleidomastoid muscle acts as a primary landmark by dividing the neck into the [___] and [___] triangles.
back: Anterior and posterior triangles. This division is essential for organizing the neurovascular structures of the neck.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: A patient following a deep neck injury exhibits a drooping shoulder and inability to shrug against resistance. This indicates a lesion of the nerve supplying the [___].
back: Trapezius muscle. The nerve involved is the spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), which crosses the posterior triangle superficially.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: How do the Trapezius and Serratus anterior muscles cooperate during abduction of the arm above 90 degrees?
back: They perform upward rotation of the scapula. The upper and lower Trapezius fibers rotate the glenoid cavity superiorly, allowing the arm to be raised above the head.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Distinguish between the origins of the sternal and clavicular heads of the Sternocleidomastoid.
back: Sternal head: Rounded tendon from the anterior manubrium sterni. Clavicular head: Fleshy fibers from the superior surface of the medial third of the clavicle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Identify the primary actions of the middle and inferior fibers of the Trapezius muscle.
back: Middle fibers: Retract (adduct) the scapula toward the midline. Inferior fibers: Depress the scapula and assist in upward rotation.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
coreConcept: Motor innervation of SCM and Trapezius
front: The motor innervation of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles is provided by the [___] nerve.
back:
- Spinal accessory nerve (Cranial Nerve XI).
- Note: Proprioceptive fibers are provided by C2, C3 (SCM) and C3, C4 (Trapezius).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: A neonate presents with the head tilted toward the right and the chin rotated toward the left following a difficult labor. This clinical presentation, caused by fibrosis of the sternocleidomastoid, is known as [___].
back:
- Congenital Torticollis (Wry neck).
- Caused by a hematoma or excessive stretching of the SCM during delivery.
- Leads to shortening of the muscle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Explain the role of the trapezius muscle during the abduction of the humerus beyond 90 degrees.
back:
- It rotates the scapula upward (superiorly).
- Acts synergistically with the serratus anterior.
- Tilts the glenoid cavity upward to allow full arm elevation.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Contrast the effect of a Spinal Accessory Nerve (CN XI) lesion in the posterior triangle versus a lesion at the jugular foramen.
back:
- Posterior triangle: Only Trapezius is paralyzed (shoulder droop); SCM is spared.
- Jugular foramen: Both SCM and Trapezius are paralyzed (inability to rotate head and shrug shoulder).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Identify the muscle that serves as the key landmark for dividing the neck into anterior and posterior triangles and list its superior attachments.
back:
- Sternocleidomastoid (SCM).
- Attachments: Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral half of the superior nuchal line.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The [___] muscle originates from the medial third of the superior nuchal line, the ligamentum nuchae, and the spines of C7-T12 vertebrae.
back:
- Trapezius.
- Insertion: Lateral third of the clavicle, acromion, and spine of the scapula.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: A patient with a deep laceration in the posterior triangle of the neck is unable to shrug their shoulder. Identify the muscle affected and its specific action that is lost.
back:
- Trapezius muscle.
- Loss of the upper fibers' action (elevation of the scapula).

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Describe the mechanical action of the sternocleidomastoid when acting unilaterally versus acting bilaterally.
back:
- Unilateral: Tilts head to same side; rotates face to opposite side.
- Bilateral: Flexes the neck (draws head forward); acts as an accessory muscle of inspiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Distinguish between the insertions of the three functional parts of the trapezius muscle.
back:
- Upper: Lateral third of the clavicle.
- Middle: Acromion and superior lip of the scapular spine.
- Lower: Apex of the scapular spine.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Identify the two separate heads of origin for the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
back:
- Sternal head: Rounded tendon from the manubrium sterni.
- Clavicular head: Fleshy fibers from the medial third of the clavicle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The sternocleidomastoid muscle inserts superiorly onto the [___] of the temporal bone and the lateral half of the superior nuchal line.
back:
Mastoid process.
- Primary superior attachment site.
- Located on the temporal bone.
- Continuous with the superior nuchal line attachment.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: A patient presents with a sagging shoulder and inability to shrug against resistance following a lymph node biopsy in the posterior triangle. The nerve likely damaged is [___].
back:
Spinal Accessory Nerve (CN XI).
- Provides motor supply to Trapezius and SCM.
- Vulnerable due to its superficial course in the posterior triangle.
- Results in trapezius paralysis.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Explain the mechanical role of the trapezius muscle in facilitating overhead abduction of the arm beyond 90 degrees.
back:
Superior rotation of the scapula.
- Upper and lower fibers act as a couple.
- Tilts the glenoid cavity upward.
- Essential for full abduction alongside the serratus anterior.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Contrast the proprioceptive nerve supply of the sternocleidomastoid with that of the trapezius muscle.
back:
Cervical nerves C2-C3 vs. C3-C4.
- SCM: Proprioception via C2 and C3.
- Trapezius: Proprioception via C3 and C4.
- Both use CN XI for motor function only.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Describe the primary mechanical outcome of bilateral contraction of the sternocleidomastoid muscles.
back:
Flexion of the cervical column.
- Pulls the head forward.
- Assists in thrusting the chin forward.
- Acts as an accessory muscle of forced inspiration.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The trapezius muscle is considered a part of the [___] group of neck muscles, supplied by the same cranial nerve as the sternocleidomastoid.
back:
Superficial (or Posterior Triangle boundary).
- Supplied by Spinal Accessory Nerve (CN XI).
- Large, diamond-shaped muscle of the back and neck.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: An infant presents with the head tilted toward the right shoulder and the chin rotated toward the left. Identify the affected muscle and the clinical diagnosis.
back:
Right Sternocleidomastoid; Congenital Torticollis.
- Caused by SCM fibrosis or birth trauma.
- Resulting shortening pulls head to same side.
- Chin rotates to the opposite (unaffected) side.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: How does unilateral contraction of the left sternocleidomastoid muscle affect head and neck orientation?
back:
Left lateral flexion and right rotation.
- Tilts head toward the left shoulder.
- Rotates the face/chin toward the right.
- Uses the mastoid process as a lever.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Distinguish the origin points of the two inferior heads of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
back:
Sternal vs. Clavicular heads.
- Sternal head: Anterior surface of the manubrium sterni.
- Clavicular head: Medial third of the superior surface of the clavicle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Enumerate the midline bony and ligamentous origins of the trapezius muscle.
back:
- External occipital protuberance.
- Medial third of superior nuchal line.
- Ligamentum nuchae.
- Spinous processes of C7 to T12 vertebrae.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: The trapezius muscle inserts onto the spine of the scapula, the acromion, and the posterior border of the [___].
back:
• Lateral third of the clavicle.
• This mirrors the origin of the deltoid muscle.
• Forms the posterior boundary of the omoclavicular triangle.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: An infant presents with the head tilted toward the right and the chin rotated toward the left. Ultrasound reveals a fibrotic mass in the neck muscle. Identify the condition and affected muscle.
back:
• Congenital Torticollis (Wry neck).
• Sternocleidomastoid (SCM) muscle.
• Results from birth trauma leading to hematoma and subsequent fibrosis/shortening.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Explain how the Trapezius facilitates full abduction of the humerus above the horizontal plane (90 degrees).
back:
• Scapular Rotation.
• The upper and lower fibers act as a force couple to rotate the glenoid cavity upward.
• Necessary for the humerus to clear the acromion.

category: Describe the attachments, actions and nerve supply of sternocleidomastoid and trapezius
front: Contrast the proprioceptive nerve supply of the Sternocleidomastoid with that of the Trapezius muscle.
back:
• Sternocleidomastoid: Ventral rami of C2 and C3.
• Trapezius: Ventral rami of C3 and C4.
• Note: Both receive motor supply from the Spinal Accessory Nerve (CN XI).
